title: GitHub - Jyotishmoy12/AgentTM
excerpt: Contribute to Jyotishmoy12/AgentTM development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
Agent Time Machine v0.1

A local Go CLI that records real, AgentTM-managed noninteractive Codex runs in SQLite, with baseline/final workspace checkpoints and historical file inspection. The embedded React/TypeScript UI displays real stored sessions, timelines, historical files, parent diffs and isolated worktree forks. This implements Milestones 0–5 in the MVP specification.

Validation status: real Windows end-to-end coding, tests, intermediate capture, CLI/UI restoration, failure and Ctrl+C cancellation passed. Automated tests, selected race checks and five browser tests pass. All six OS/architecture release targets build; Windows installation was tested. Remote CI and native Linux/macOS execution are configured but not claimed as observed here. See release evidence, Codex compatibility, snapshots, UI/API, and fork safety/recovery.

Release installation

Local archives are generated under dist/0.1.0/. Select the archive for your OS and architecture, verify it against the matching SHA256SUMS, and extract the single executable. Git 2.42+ and an authenticated Codex CLI are required for recording. Go and Node are not needed to run the release executable.

The local installers verify archive checksums before installing; they do not download anything. Windows example:

.\scripts\install.ps1 -Archive .\dist\0.1.0\agenttm_0.1.0_windows_amd64.zip -AddToPath

PATH changes require -AddToPath; upgrades require -Force. If script execution is disabled, extract the ZIP and invoke agenttm.exe directly. On Unix use sh scripts/install.sh archive.tar.gz [install-directory].

Open your recorded history

From your initialized Git repository:

$agenttm = 'C:\dev\AgentTM\bin\agenttm.exe'
& $agenttm ui

AgentTM opens http://127.0.0.1:7331 in your browser. Keep the terminal running; Ctrl+C stops the server. If the port is occupied, use & $agenttm ui --port 7332. For an installed-app style launch with a Codex readiness check, run & $agenttm desktop. It opens the same local UI and reports whether Codex is installed and authenticated; existing history remains available when Codex is not ready. Use --no-browser to print the URL without opening it. No Node installation is needed to run the prebuilt executable; all production assets are embedded.

Select a session, then a timeline event or checkpoint. Files shows the historical tree and read-only Monaco viewer. Compare with parent shows changed paths and unified patches. Activity shows sanitized event input/output and the observed checkpoint. An event without a checkpoint displays the last known workspace with an explicit label; events preceding the baseline show no state. Fork checkpoint shows the exact destination, branch and partial-snapshot warnings before confirmation. Restored files live under .agenttm/worktrees/; the original working tree, index and HEAD stay unchanged. No restored code runs.

Build and test (PowerShell)

Requires Go 1.25+, Git and an installed/authenticated Codex CLI. SQLite is bundled through a pure Go driver; no SQLite install or C compiler is required.

cd C:\dev\AgentTM
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build -o .\bin\agenttm.exe .\cmd\agenttm
.\bin\agenttm.exe version
.\bin\agenttm.exe codex doctor

On macOS/Linux: go build -o bin/agenttm ./cmd/agenttm.

The checked-in assets under internal/server/ui allow Go-only builds. After changing frontend source, rebuild the embedded assets first (Node 24+):

Set-Location C:\dev\AgentTM\web
npm.cmd ci
npm.cmd test
npm.cmd run build
Set-Location ..
go build -o .\bin\agenttm.exe .\cmd\agenttm

Try it in a disposable repository

The source folder need not be a Git repository to build the executable. The repository you record must be a Git working tree. No commit is required.

$agenttm = 'C:\dev\AgentTM\bin\agenttm.exe'
$demo = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('agenttm-demo-' + [guid]::NewGuid())
New-Item -ItemType Directory $demo | Out-Null
Set-Location $demo
git init
& $agenttm init
& $agenttm doctor
Set-Content -LiteralPath snapshot-demo.txt -Value 'Original content'
& $agenttm run codex --model gpt-6.1-sol -- "Reply with a short greeting. Do not change files."
& $agenttm sessions
# Copy the session UUID shown above:
& $agenttm events '<session-id>'
& $agenttm events '<session-id>' --after 10 --limit 50
& $agenttm checkpoints '<session-id>'
# Copy the baseline checkpoint UUID shown above:
& $agenttm cat '<baseline-id>' snapshot-demo.txt

# Explicitly observe a manual change, without another model request:
Set-Content -LiteralPath snapshot-demo.txt -Value 'Changed content'
& $agenttm checkpoint '<session-id>'
# Copy the new checkpoint UUID:
& $agenttm diff '<new-checkpoint-id>'
& $agenttm cat '<baseline-id>' snapshot-demo.txt   # still Original content
& $agenttm cat '<new-checkpoint-id>' snapshot-demo.txt
& $agenttm show '<new-checkpoint-id>'
& $agenttm fork '<new-checkpoint-id>' --name alternative
& $agenttm forks

If your configured model is unavailable, explicitly choose one available to your Codex account (this does not change global settings):

& $agenttm run codex --model '<available-model>' -- "Reply with a short greeting."

Then try a real coding task in that disposable repo. Codex's existing permissions, sandbox, rules, hooks and authentication apply. AgentTM does not grant write access or bypass approval policy. Tasks may fail or be refused under those policies. Ctrl+C cancels the child process tree and attempts to persist cancellation status. The default honors Codex's existing sandbox/approval configuration. To explicitly allow a coding task to write inside a disposable repository:

& $agenttm run codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --sandbox workspace-write --snapshot-after-tool=true -- "Implement a small function and test it."

read-only is the other supported explicit sandbox override. No unsafe bypass flags are passed. New configs enable best-effort scans near supported completed command/file-change items; older config values are preserved. Use the flag above or capture.snapshot_after_tool to enable them. They do not pause Codex or prove per-tool causality. The final workspace scan uses a separate two-minute cleanup context, including after cancellation or Codex failure. No change means the existing checkpoint is reused; the final observation event still links to it. Older Phase 1 sessions have no historical files. checkpoint observes the workspace now, even when linked to an older session; it does not reconstruct its past.

Use & $agenttm in PowerShell; assigning a path to a variable does not install a bare agenttm command. codex --version must also work in that terminal. If Codex is only bundled with VS Code, add its executable directory to that terminal's $env:PATH, or install the standalone CLI.

Available commands

Command Behavior
init Idempotent config, directories, SQLite migrations and local Git exclusion
version Version and build commit
codex doctor Version, JSON capability and observable login readiness
doctor Repository/config/database checks and Codex readiness
run codex [--model MODEL] -- "task" Supervise real Codex and persist sanitized JSONL observations
sessions List sessions, UTC timestamps, status and exit code
events <id> [--after N] [--limit N] JSONL events ordered by per-session sequence; default 100, maximum 1000
checkpoints <session-id> Checkpoint IDs, kind, time, files and partial flags
checkpoint <session-id> Manually observe the current workspace; reuse unchanged state
show <checkpoint-id> Versioned manifest, file tree, hashes, modes and omissions as JSON
cat <checkpoint-id> <path> Verified historical UTF-8 text, maximum 1 MiB output
diff <checkpoint-id> JSON changes and bounded unified patches against parent (empty tree for baseline)
fork <checkpoint-id> --name NAME [--allow-partial] Restore and verify a new isolated worktree
forks List ready, restoring or failed fork records
purge --session ID [--yes] Confirm logical deletion of an ended, unforked session; retain shared blobs
ui [--port N] [--no-browser] Serve embedded read-only history on loopback and open your browser

Unknown commands return exit code 2; operational failures return 1. Normal child failure codes are forwarded; cancellation returns 130. Recording/protocol failure returns nonzero even if the child exits zero. JSONL goes to stdout, recording status to stderr. No executable or fixture simulates Codex during ordinary CLI usage.

Storage and privacy

init resolves the canonical Git root even from nested directories. It creates .agenttm/config.json, data/events.db, objects/, and logs/. The SQLite store uses transactions, foreign keys, WAL and a busy timeout. Snapshots use SHA-256 objects and versioned JSON manifests under .agenttm/manifests/; SQLite indexes the manifest checksum and checkpoint/event links. Logs contain only a session outcome summary. Schema 1 databases migrate automatically without losing events.

Only .git/info/exclude is updated, with /.agenttm/. Tracked .gitignore, the index and HEAD are untouched. Existing local storage symlinks are rejected. Restrictive modes are requested on POSIX; Windows ACLs are inherited. Other users with filesystem access can read the local recording data.

Prompt capture defaults to metadata_only. The complete task text is removed if echoed in event strings; fragments/paraphrases may still appear in outputs. To opt into sanitized prompt storage set capture.prompt_mode to sanitized in config. Prompts use stdin rather than OS process arguments. Raw events are not persisted. Known credential patterns are redacted before storage; this is best-effort and cannot identify every secret. Review recordings before sharing them. File objects preserve exact bytes and are not content-redacted. Snapshot privacy depends on filename/directory exclusions; credentials embedded in source code can still be captured. Inspect show for exclusions and partial flags.

Event storage uses an allowlist of observable fields. Reasoning item text and unknown event bodies are omitted. Payloads are bounded by capture.max_event_payload_bytes (default 64 KiB), with explicit truncation flags. Malformed/oversized JSONL lines produce omission records; parsing resumes at the next line. Raw stderr is drained to a discard sink for privacy, so startup failures that appear only on stderr require a direct Codex diagnostic run. No AgentTM telemetry or uploads are implemented; Codex itself uses its configured service.

Current limits

  • Only runs launched through agenttm run codex are captured. Existing interactive sessions are not observed.
  • Baseline/final/manual scans and optional completed-tool observations capture scan-time state; continuous or deterministic per-tool history is not claimed. Failed restore directories are retained for diagnosis.
  • Events are observations, not a complete tool trace or proof of file authorship. Separate receipts get separate UUIDs/sequences; no payload-hash deduplication.
  • Graceful Ctrl+C is handled. Forced AgentTM termination or machine failure can leave a session active; doctor reports active sessions without assuming that a separate recorder has died. No crash-recovery rewrite is attempted.
  • doctor checks SQLite, manifests, object hashes and observation links. Interrupted writes can leave unreferenced files or a stale snapshot lock; these are reported without automatic deletion. See the snapshot recovery guide.
  • Automated tests use synthetic subprocesses explicitly labeled as test fixtures. Actual Codex schema/failure evidence and remaining acceptance checks are in the compatibility document. CI is configured for Windows, Linux and macOS; remote CI execution has not been observed here.

Build release archives

go run ./cmd/release --version 0.1.0 --out dist/0.1.0

Rebuild the frontend first after UI source edits. The packager creates Windows, Linux and macOS archives for amd64/arm64 plus SHA256SUMS, notices and restore guidance. Existing outputs are refused; use a new output directory for a new build. CI runs native tests across all three OSes and browser tests on Linux. A version tag or manual release workflow publishes the individual archives to the repository's GitHub Releases page, so users can download only their platform's archive.

Deferred beyond v0.1: interactive Codex capture, additional agents, automatic continuation, cloud sync, encrypted backup, and blob garbage collection.

content_html_zh:
Agent Time Machine v0.1

A local Go CLI that records real, AgentTM-managed noninteractive Codex runs in SQLite, with baseline/final workspace checkpoints and historical file inspection. The embedded React/TypeScript UI displays real stored sessions, timelines, historical files, parent diffs and isolated worktree forks. This implements Milestones 0–5 in the MVP specification.

Validation status: real Windows end-to-end coding, tests, intermediate capture, CLI/UI restoration, failure and Ctrl+C cancellation passed. Automated tests, selected race checks and five browser tests pass. All six OS/architecture release targets build; Windows installation was tested. Remote CI and native Linux/macOS execution are configured but not claimed as observed here. See release evidence, Codex compatibility, snapshots, UI/API, and fork safety/recovery.

Release installation

Local archives are generated under dist/0.1.0/. Select the archive for your OS and architecture, verify it against the matching SHA256SUMS, and extract the single executable. Git 2.42+ and an authenticated Codex CLI are required for recording. Go and Node are not needed to run the release executable.

The local installers verify archive checksums before installing; they do not download anything. Windows example:

.\scripts\install.ps1 -Archive .\dist\0.1.0\agenttm_0.1.0_windows_amd64.zip -AddToPath

PATH changes require -AddToPath; upgrades require -Force. If script execution is disabled, extract the ZIP and invoke agenttm.exe directly. On Unix use sh scripts/install.sh archive.tar.gz [install-directory].

Open your recorded history

From your initialized Git repository:

$agenttm = 'C:\dev\AgentTM\bin\agenttm.exe'
& $agenttm ui

AgentTM opens http://127.0.0.1:7331 in your browser. Keep the terminal running; Ctrl+C stops the server. If the port is occupied, use & $agenttm ui --port 7332. For an installed-app style launch with a Codex readiness check, run & $agenttm desktop. It opens the same local UI and reports whether Codex is installed and authenticated; existing history remains available when Codex is not ready. Use --no-browser to print the URL without opening it. No Node installation is needed to run the prebuilt executable; all production assets are embedded.

Select a session, then a timeline event or checkpoint. Files shows the historical tree and read-only Monaco viewer. Compare with parent shows changed paths and unified patches. Activity shows sanitized event input/output and the observed checkpoint. An event without a checkpoint displays the last known workspace with an explicit label; events preceding the baseline show no state. Fork checkpoint shows the exact destination, branch and partial-snapshot warnings before confirmation. Restored files live under .agenttm/worktrees/; the original working tree, index and HEAD stay unchanged. No restored code runs.

Build and test (PowerShell)

Requires Go 1.25+, Git and an installed/authenticated Codex CLI. SQLite is bundled through a pure Go driver; no SQLite install or C compiler is required.

cd C:\dev\AgentTM
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build -o .\bin\agenttm.exe .\cmd\agenttm
.\bin\agenttm.exe version
.\bin\agenttm.exe codex doctor

On macOS/Linux: go build -o bin/agenttm ./cmd/agenttm.

The checked-in assets under internal/server/ui allow Go-only builds. After changing frontend source, rebuild the embedded assets first (Node 24+):

Set-Location C:\dev\AgentTM\web
npm.cmd ci
npm.cmd test
npm.cmd run build
Set-Location ..
go build -o .\bin\agenttm.exe .\cmd\agenttm

Try it in a disposable repository

The source folder need not be a Git repository to build the executable. The repository you record must be a Git working tree. No commit is required.

$agenttm = 'C:\dev\AgentTM\bin\agenttm.exe'
$demo = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('agenttm-demo-' + [guid]::NewGuid())
New-Item -ItemType Directory $demo | Out-Null
Set-Location $demo
git init
& $agenttm init
& $agenttm doctor
Set-Content -LiteralPath snapshot-demo.txt -Value 'Original content'
& $agenttm run codex --model gpt-6.1-sol -- "Reply with a short greeting. Do not change files."
& $agenttm sessions
# Copy the session UUID shown above:
& $agenttm events '<session-id>'
& $agenttm events '<session-id>' --after 10 --limit 50
& $agenttm checkpoints '<session-id>'
# Copy the baseline checkpoint UUID shown above:
& $agenttm cat '<baseline-id>' snapshot-demo.txt

# Explicitly observe a manual change, without another model request:
Set-Content -LiteralPath snapshot-demo.txt -Value 'Changed content'
& $agenttm checkpoint '<session-id>'
# Copy the new checkpoint UUID:
& $agenttm diff '<new-checkpoint-id>'
& $agenttm cat '<baseline-id>' snapshot-demo.txt   # still Original content
& $agenttm cat '<new-checkpoint-id>' snapshot-demo.txt
& $agenttm show '<new-checkpoint-id>'
& $agenttm fork '<new-checkpoint-id>' --name alternative
& $agenttm forks

If your configured model is unavailable, explicitly choose one available to your Codex account (this does not change global settings):

& $agenttm run codex --model '<available-model>' -- "Reply with a short greeting."

Then try a real coding task in that disposable repo. Codex's existing permissions, sandbox, rules, hooks and authentication apply. AgentTM does not grant write access or bypass approval policy. Tasks may fail or be refused under those policies. Ctrl+C cancels the child process tree and attempts to persist cancellation status. The default honors Codex's existing sandbox/approval configuration. To explicitly allow a coding task to write inside a disposable repository:

& $agenttm run codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --sandbox workspace-write --snapshot-after-tool=true -- "Implement a small function and test it."

read-only is the other supported explicit sandbox override. No unsafe bypass flags are passed. New configs enable best-effort scans near supported completed command/file-change items; older config values are preserved. Use the flag above or capture.snapshot_after_tool to enable them. They do not pause Codex or prove per-tool causality. The final workspace scan uses a separate two-minute cleanup context, including after cancellation or Codex failure. No change means the existing checkpoint is reused; the final observation event still links to it. Older Phase 1 sessions have no historical files. checkpoint observes the workspace now, even when linked to an older session; it does not reconstruct its past.

Use & $agenttm in PowerShell; assigning a path to a variable does not install a bare agenttm command. codex --version must also work in that terminal. If Codex is only bundled with VS Code, add its executable directory to that terminal's $env:PATH, or install the standalone CLI.

Storage and privacy

init resolves the canonical Git root even from nested directories. It creates .agenttm/config.json, data/events.db, objects/, and logs/. The SQLite store uses transactions, foreign keys, WAL and a busy timeout. Snapshots use SHA-256 objects and versioned JSON manifests under .agenttm/manifests/; SQLite indexes the manifest checksum and checkpoint/event links. Logs contain only a session outcome summary. Schema 1 databases migrate automatically without losing events.

Only .git/info/exclude is updated, with /.agenttm/. Tracked .gitignore, the index and HEAD are untouched. Existing local storage symlinks are rejected. Restrictive modes are requested on POSIX; Windows ACLs are inherited. Other users with filesystem access can read the local recording data.

Prompt capture defaults to metadata_only. The complete task text is removed if echoed in event strings; fragments/paraphrases may still appear in outputs. To opt into sanitized prompt storage set capture.prompt_mode to sanitized in config. Prompts use stdin rather than OS process arguments. Raw events are not persisted. Known credential patterns are redacted before storage; this is best-effort and cannot identify every secret. Review recordings before sharing them. File objects preserve exact bytes and are not content-redacted. Snapshot privacy depends on filename/directory exclusions; credentials embedded in source code can still be captured. Inspect show for exclusions and partial flags.

Event storage uses an allowlist of observable fields. Reasoning item text and unknown event bodies are omitted. Payloads are bounded by capture.max_event_payload_bytes (default 64 KiB), with explicit truncation flags. Malformed/oversized JSONL lines produce omission records; parsing resumes at the next line. Raw stderr is drained to a discard sink for privacy, so startup failures that appear only on stderr require a direct Codex diagnostic run. No AgentTM telemetry or uploads are implemented; Codex itself uses its configured service.

Current limits

  • Only runs launched through agenttm run codex are captured. Existing interactive sessions are not observed.
  • Baseline/final/manual scans and optional completed-tool observations capture scan-time state; continuous or deterministic per-tool history is not claimed. Failed restore directories are retained for diagnosis.
  • Events are observations, not a complete tool trace or proof of file authorship. Separate receipts get separate UUIDs/sequences; no payload-hash deduplication.
  • Graceful Ctrl+C is handled. Forced AgentTM termination or machine failure can leave a session active; doctor reports active sessions without assuming that a separate recorder has died. No crash-recovery rewrite is attempted.
  • doctor checks SQLite, manifests, object hashes and observation links. Interrupted writes can leave unreferenced files or a stale snapshot lock; these are reported without automatic deletion. See the snapshot recovery guide.
  • Automated tests use synthetic subprocesses explicitly labeled as test fixtures. Actual Codex schema/failure evidence and remaining acceptance checks are in the compatibility document. CI is configured for Windows, Linux and macOS; remote CI execution has not been observed here.

Build release archives

go run ./cmd/release --version 0.1.0 --out dist/0.1.0

Rebuild the frontend first after UI source edits. The packager creates Windows, Linux and macOS archives for amd64/arm64 plus SHA256SUMS, notices and restore guidance. Existing outputs are refused; use a new output directory for a new build. CI runs native tests across all three OSes and browser tests on Linux. A version tag or manual release workflow publishes the individual archives to the repository's GitHub Releases page, so users can download only their platform's archive.

Deferred beyond v0.1: interactive Codex capture, additional agents, automatic continuation, cloud sync, encrypted backup, and blob garbage collection.
